mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 330i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 330i engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £6,500 supply-only, depending on the engine code and condition type. Used engines: £600-£3,000 (M54/N52/N53) to £1,500-£3,000 (N55/B48). Reconditioned engines: £1,800-£5,000. Rebuilt engines: £2,800-£6,500 with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit adds approximately £650-£1,200 in labour depending on the generation.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 3 Series 330i?

acceptedAnswer.text: On B48 and N-series 330i engines, the key warning signs are: a rattling or clacking noise from the front of the engine on cold start, a whining noise that increases with engine RPM, rough idle or misfires, and engine management light with timing-related fault codes. If you hear any of these, get the car inspected immediately - catching it early can save your engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 330i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the age and value of your car. E46 330i (worth £3,000-£8,000): repair if possible; full rebuild only if the car is exceptional. E90 330i (worth £3,000-£10,000): timing chain repair or used engine often makes sense. F30 330i (worth £6,000-£16,000): rebuilt engine with warranty is usually a sound investment. G20 330i (worth £15,000-£35,000): replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. Always compare the cost of replacement against your car's current market value before deciding.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 330i and 340i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 330i and 340i are different engine families entirely. 330i (F30/G20): B48 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo, 252-258 hp. 340i (F30/G20): B58 3.0-litre straight-six turbo, 320-382 hp. The 340i uses the larger six-cylinder B58 engine - more power, more torque, but higher running costs and a more expensive replacement.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 330i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 330i engine replacement takes 2-5 working days. E46/E90 (M54/N52/N53): 10-14 hours labour - around 2-3 days. F30/G20 (N55/B48): 8-12 hours labour - around 2-3 days. Supply-only engines can be delivered nationwide within 1-2 working days. Full supply & fit typically adds 1-2 days for booking and workshop scheduling.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW 3 Series 330i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every rebuilt BMW 3 Series 330i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty as standard. The warranty covers manufacturing defects and parts failure. Upgraded components address the original failure points (e.g. improved timing chain guides on B48). Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 330i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 330i has been the performance benchmark of the 3 Series petrol range since its debut in the E46 generation. Over four generations, the 330i badge has moved from a naturally aspirated 3.0-litre straight-six (M54) to the high-output N52, the direct-injection N53, the turbocharged N55, and finally the modular B48 turbo-four - each iteration delivering more power, efficiency and refinement than the last.

milestones.description: M54B30, 3.0-litre straight-six (231 hp) - E46 generation, naturally aspirated
N52B30, 3.0-litre straight-six (258 hp) - E90/E91/E92/E93 generation, magnesium-aluminium composite block
N53B30, 3.0-litre straight-six (268 hp) - E90 LCI/E92/E93, direct injection
N55B30, 3.0-litre straight-six turbo (306 hp) - F30 generation, TwinPower Turbo
B48B20O0, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo (252 hp) - F30 LCI, modular engine family
B48B20O1, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo (258 hp) - G20 generation, updated

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 330i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 3.0L Petrol (2000-2005)
items.commonFailure: The M54B30 is generally robust, but VANOS solenoid failure and oil leaks from the valve cover gasket are common on higher-mileage units. Cooling system components (water pump, expansion tank, radiator) degrade with age and can cause overheating.

items.title: 3.0L Petrol (2005-2007)
items.commonFailure: Valve stem seal wear causes excessive oil consumption - blue smoke on start-up is the telltale sign. The electric water pump is a known failure point; failure leads to rapid overheating.

items.title: 3.0L Petrol (2007-2012)
items.commonFailure: High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure is a known issue on the N53. Direct-injection injectors can also fail, causing misfires. Timing chain tensioner wear has been reported, though less frequently than on N-series four-cylinder engines.

items.title: 3.0L Turbo Petrol (2012-2016)
items.commonFailure: The N55 is generally more reliable than its N54 predecessor, but VANOS solenoid failure and oil leaks from the valve cover gasket are common. The charge pipe can crack under boost, causing a loss of power.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 330i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 3 Series 330i's inline-six and turbo-four engines are renowned for their smooth power delivery and reliability, but age and mileage bring common failure points. Timing chain wear affects the B48 and some N-series engines, while oil consumption and VANOS issues plague the naturally aspirated six-cylinders. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the BMW 3 Series 330i B48 and N-Series Engines Need Attention
problems.rootCause: On B48 engines, the timing chain can experience premature wear due to tensioner or guide failure. On N-series engines, the chain can stretch over time.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early - rattle on start-up but no performance loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If timing has jumped or engine is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 330i is worth between £3,000 and £35,000 depending on generation, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. For E46/E90 examples under £5,000, a used engine or timing chain repair may offer better value than a full rebuilt unit. For F30/G20 cars worth £10,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, get it inspected immediately. Replacing the timing chain and tensioner before failure costs £800-£1,800 at a specialist and can save your engine. If the engine has already jumped timing, a full replacement is usually the most cost-effective route - a specialist rebuild with upgraded components costs less than a dealer replacement and carries a 12-month warranty.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B48/N-series BMW 3 Series 330i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption and Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series 330i N52 Engine Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: Valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability, allowing oil to seep past the valves into the combustion chamber. The valve cover gasket also deteriorates over time, causing external leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals - can often be done without removing the cylinder head
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is the only issue
If external oil leaks are present
If oil consumption is severe or other issues exist

problems.vehicleValueCheck: An E90-generation BMW 3 Series 330i (2005-2007) is typically worth £3,000-£8,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. Valve stem seal replacement at £800-£1,500 is usually justified. A full rebuild is only worthwhile if the car is otherwise in excellent condition.
problems.recommendation: For N52 330i owners, monitor oil consumption carefully. If you're adding more than 1 litre per 1,000 miles, valve stem seal replacement is the cost-effective fix. A full rebuilt engine is only justified if the car is otherwise in excellent condition and you plan to keep it.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N52 BMW 3 Series 330i engine prices

problems.group: VANOS Solenoid and Cooling System Failures
problems.h4: VANOS Solenoid and Cooling System Failures - Why the BMW 3 Series 330i Loses Power and Overheats
problems.rootCause: VANOS solenoids become clogged with oil debris, affecting variable valve timing and causing rough idling, reduced power, and poor fuel economy. The electric water pump on N-series engines is a known failure point, leading to rapid overheating if not replaced.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Clean or replace solenoids; oil change
repairOptions.longevity: If rough idle or reduced power is present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For E46 and E90 330i owners, these repairs are routine maintenance and well within the value of the car. Addressing them early prevents more costly engine damage.
problems.recommendation: For M54 and N52 330i owners, preventative cooling system maintenance is the smart play. Replacing the water pump and thermostat at 60,000 miles costs far less than an engine replacement if a leak leads to overheating. VANOS solenoid cleaning is a simple DIY-friendly job that restores lost performance.
